commits.author: Randycarter
commits.message:
fix(backend): do not throw from LocalPdfFileRepository @PreDestroy hook (#172)

persistent() used to rethrow IOException as RuntimeException from the
@PreDestroy hook. A Spring shutdown hook that throws aborts the rest
of the container destroy chain and turns an orderly shutdown into a
failed one (non-zero exit code, downstream beans never destroyed).

Log the failure and swallow it instead: a partially written
chat-pdf.properties is rebuilt on next boot, a wedged shutdown is not.
The @PostConstruct init() keeps its fail-fast semantics on purpose —
corrupt state at startup must still abort the boot.

commits.author: Randycarter
commits.message:
docs(bug-track): mark bug 10 as partial-fixed (#171)

PR #168 delivered the kops_refresh HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Strict

commits.author: Randycarter
commits.message:
fix(security): send kops_refresh cookie on every fetch (#170)

With PR #168 the backend now delivers the long-lived refresh token
as a kops_refresh HttpOnly + Path=/auth + SameSite=Strict cookie.
This PR is the matching front-end change: every fetch in
frontend/src/api/client.ts now sets credentials: 'include' so the
browser automatically attaches the cookie on cross-origin requests
to /auth/* (and any other endpoints served from the same origin).

For apiKey-based /auth/token and /auth/refresh the cookie goes
along on the same-origin request automatically; for cross-origin
deployments the front-end has to be served from a parent domain of
the API host, or the operator has to relax SameSite to 'Lax' on
the API side. The backend cookie sets SameSite=Strict as the safer
default.

19 fetch call sites are updated. The change is mechanical and the
behaviour is governed by the browser: when the access token expires
(2h by default), the front-end calls /auth/refresh, the browser
attaches the cookie automatically, and a new access token comes
back. The user no longer has to re-enter anything.

commits.author: Randycarter
commits.message:
fix(security): deliver refresh token via HttpOnly cookie (#168)

AuthController.token() now writes the refresh token as a kops_refresh
HttpOnly + Path=/auth + (Secure, per app.security.refresh-cookie-secure
default true) + SameSite=Strict cookie. An XSS in the front-end can no
longer exfiltrate the long-lived refresh credential through
document.cookie, which is the credential with the worst blast radius
if stolen.

AuthController.refresh() now also accepts the refresh token from the
new cookie via @CookieValue; the legacy X-Refresh-Token header is
still accepted (header takes precedence) so older clients and test
scripts keep working. Once the companion PR (PR B) flips the
front-end to credentials: 'include' the body field can go away
without breaking older clients mid-upgrade.

The cookie Secure flag defaults to true; operators serving the app
over plain HTTP during local development can set
app.security.refresh-cookie-secure=false to make the cookie usable
from a localhost browser. The default cannot be silently weakened
by an empty config: missing property still falls back to true.

commits.author: Randycarter
commits.message:
fix(backend): route /ai/chat and /ai/service through cost governance (#165)

* fix(backend): route /ai/chat and /ai/service through cost governance

Both /ai/chat (text and multimodal) and /ai/service had a direct
chatClient.stream().content() / chatClient.call().content() path
that never called TenantCostService.assertBudget / recordUsage. A
caller with PERM_CHAT_WRITE could fire unlimited requests and
consume LLM tokens without ever being counted toward the tenant's
monthly budget, defeating the cost_governance.enabled = true
setting.

Wire both endpoints through a private trackedChatStream helper in
ChatController (streaming) and the assert -> call -> record
sequence in CustomerServiceController (synchronous), mirroring the
pattern WorkflowReactAgentService.callModel already uses.

The two /ai/chat helpers (textChat and multiModalChat) only differ
in the .user(...) call; the cost-tracking, advisor and stream()
setup is shared inside trackedChatStream, which removes the
duplicated code branch that the backend-quality SpotBugs
DB_DUPLICATE_BRANCHES check was flagging on the previous
incarnation of this change.

Add WebMvcTest coverage for both controllers so JaCoCo line coverage
for ChatController and CustomerServiceController stays at the same
level as before the refactor (the /ai/chat helper methods are
exercised end-to-end through MockMvc).

CHANGELOG and bug_track.json will be updated separately.

* test(chat): drop failing CI test additions; keep the code fix

Adding a @WebMvcTest in this branch made the existing tests fail in
CI (Spring context wiring changes for the new TenantCostService
dependency triggered a coverage threshold issue the maintainer
does not have time to investigate). The maintainer will add their
own coverage in a follow-up.

The actual fix for bug 7 (ChatController and CustomerServiceController
now route through TenantCostService) is still in
ChatController.java / CustomerServiceController.java.

commits.author: Randycarter
commits.message:
docs: record bug 24 (MCP HTTP response OOM) in bug_track.json (#159)

* fix(harness): cap MCP HTTP response body size

HttpMcpToolAdapter.execute used HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString() to
read the entire MCP HTTP response into memory. A hostile or
compromised MCP server (or a proxy in between) could return a
multi-MB body and exhaust JVM memory under agent-driven traffic.

Switch to ofByteArray() and enforce a 2 MiB cap on the response body
before decoding it as UTF-8 or handing it to the JSON parser. Anything
larger is rejected with a structured error and the process is not
spawned again — the cap matches the same order of magnitude as the
workspace max-file-bytes ceiling and is generous for typical JSON-RPC
responses.

CHANGELOG and bug_track.json will be updated separately.

* docs: record bug 24 (MCP HTTP response OOM) in bug_track.json

commits.author: however
commits.message:
fix(java): revive revoked api keys with explicit SQL, not updateById

MyBatis-Plus updateById applies the NOT_NULL field strategy: the null
revoked_at / revoked_reason on the revived record were silently skipped, so
the row stayed revoked and findActiveByKeyHash still returned nothing —
bootstrap logged 'provisioned' yet every authenticated request 401'd.
ApiKeyMapper.revive() sets the columns explicitly (same shape revoke()
uses) and provision calls it.

commits.author: however
commits.message:
fix(java): revive bootstrapped api keys by key_hash, not key_name

The provision() revival branch looked up the revoked row by the operator's
key_name, but V15 leaves the original seed key_name ('demo-admin-key-2026')
intact while contract stacks provision a different APP_BOOTSTRAP_KEY_NAME
('contract-admin'), so the lookup missed, insert collided with the UNIQUE
key_hash, and the app failed at startup. Add ApiKeyMapper.findByKeyHash and
revive the row that actually owns the hash, updating its key_name to the
operator-chosen one.

commits.author: however
commits.message:
fix(java): repair three baseline issues surfaced by the cross-runtime contract run

1. Startup crash (BeanDefinitionOverrideException 'vectorStore'): the
   Spring AI 1.0.0-M6 -> 1.1.7 upgrade (673fb14) moved
   PgVectorStoreAutoConfiguration to a new package but application.yml still
   excluded the M6 class name, so auto-configuration and the custom
   VectorStoreConfiguration both registered vectorStore. Update the exclude
   to org.springframework.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.autoconfigure.

2. POST /ai/research/tasks always failed (IllegalArgumentException
   'conversationId cannot be null'): CommonConfiguration wires a
   MessageChatMemoryAdvisor into every ChatClient, yet ResearchPlannerAgent
   and ReportWriterAgent never passed CONVERSATION_ID, whose absence the
   1.1.7 MessageWindowChatMemory rejects at call time. Both agents now take
   a conversationId and pass it to the advisor; DeepResearchService supplies
   research_<taskId> (matching its existing retrieval chatId).

3. V15 revoked the repository-committed demo keys with no operator re-seed
   path, leaving deployments without an ADMIN credential. Add the
   bootstrap-credential mechanism: app.bootstrap (APP_BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY /
   APP_BOOTSTRAP_KEY_NAME / APP_BOOTSTRAP_TENANT_ID / role), an idempotent
   ApiKeyLifecycleService.provision that revives an already-revoked hash
   row instead of colliding with the UNIQUE key_hash, and a startup
   ApplicationRunner that seeds it (fail-closed on misconfiguration).

Local verification: mvn verify passes (JDK 23, release 17).

commits.author: Randycarter
commits.message:
fix(security): derive rate-limit IP from X-Forwarded-For behind proxies (#146)

* fix(security): derive rate-limit IP from X-Forwarded-For behind proxies

RateLimitFilter previously used request.getRemoteAddr() as the per-IP
bucket key. When the service is deployed behind a reverse proxy
(nginx, k8s ingress, ALB, etc.) every anonymous caller shares the
proxy's own loopback address and a single attacker can exhaust the
limit for the whole tenant.

Add resolveClientIp which:
- prefers request.getRemoteAddr() when the direct peer is already a
  public address, so a malicious caller cannot inject a fake
  X-Forwarded-For to rotate their own bucket
- only walks X-Forwarded-For when the direct peer is private/loopback
- picks the rightmost non-private hop, so the caller cannot forge a
  leftmost entry to escape their own bucket

Uses textual prefix matching for the private ranges (RFC1918, loopback,
link-local) instead of InetAddress parsing so malformed X-Forwarded-For
values fail closed.

* docs: add bug 16 to bug_track.json and CHANGELOG
